Adjusted read incorporating SLOOS: The July 2021 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to broadly supportive credit conditions—banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans across small, middle-market, and large firms, higher borrower inquiries, and easing terms for C&I loans; consumer credit standards also eased. Foreign banks likewise reported stronger C&I demand tied to inventory, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A needs. This strengthening in both loan demand and supply reinforces the FOMC’s assessment that financial conditions are accommodative and that the flow of credit to households and businesses remains supportive. It also provides fundamental backing for the Committee’s “taper soon” signal, as improving credit intermediation suggests the recovery is more self-sustaining.

Balanced against this, the statement’s acknowledgement of elevated (largely transitory) inflation, virus-related risks, and the mild hawkish tilt on asset purchases, along with Financial Stability Report concerns about elevated asset valuations and nonbank vulnerabilities, tempers the outlook.

Net: relative to the initial FSR-tilted read, SLOOS nudges the assessment more positive given improving bank lending conditions and stronger credit demand.
